summary: Renate Syed is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Renato Dávalos works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at UAM, UNAM, El Colegio de México, and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cologne (2019–2023), before becoming a Researcher Fellow at the CNRS (2023–2026).
Renjo Akamatsu (1841–1919) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.

Renshan Yang (1837–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897) and Jetavana Hermitage (1908). In 1910, he founded and served as head of the Buddhist Research Society.
René Daumal (1908–1944) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the Lycée Henri-IV (~1925–1927) and the Sorbonne (~1927–1929).

René Fohalle (1899–1984) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Liège and under Joseph Mansion, Antoine Meillet, and Émile Benveniste. He served as Professor ordinarius at the University of Liège from 1929 to 1969.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1977). He later served at Helsinki, becoming an emeritus professor in 2016.

René Grousset (1885–1952) studied at the University of Montpellier (~1903–1906). He worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, serving as head curator of Musée Cernuschi (1933) and the Guimet Museum (1945).
René Guénon (1886–1951) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at École Polytechnique, the University of Paris, the Sorbonne, and under Sylvain Lévi (~1919–1921).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Vienna, Charles University, Humboldt, and SOAS, later serving as Privatdozent at the University of Vienna (1955) and at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).

Reo Fortune (1903–1979) studied at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Cambridge under Thomas Callan Hodson (~1926–1927). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1947–1970).

Reuben Burrow (1747–1792) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He worked at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich (~1770–1774), the Tower of London (~1775–1782), and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1792).

Reuven Kahane (1931–2003) studied at UC Berkeley under Neil Smelser (~1966–1970), earning a Ph.D. In the fields of Indology and sociology, he served as Lecturer and Professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1971–2003).

Revilo Pendleton Oliver (1908–1994), an Indologist and classics scholar, earned his Ph.D. under William Abbott Oldfather at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he later served as professor from 1945 until 1977.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi (1935–2021) was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and later served there as Head of Sahityavidya (~1977–1995).

Rewata Dhamma (1929–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1956–1967) and completed a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Ria Kloppenborg (1945–2003) studied under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (Ph.D. 1974). A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, she held posts at Utrecht University (1970–1979, 1988) and the University of Groningen (1979–1988).

Richa Negi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Kurukshetra University and MNNIT Allahabad (Ph.D. 2013), and was attested as Head of Department at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts in 2026.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (attested 1988).

Richard B. Mahoney works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He studied at the University of Canterbury under MA supervisor Paul Harrison (graduating in 2002), where he also held a post attested in 2001.
